climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Riesling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
